account.name: Coldwater Freight
account.industry: transportation, logistics, supply chain and storage

dossier.summary: Coldwater Freight runs refrigerated trucking for grocery distributors, with about 300 trucks and its own brokerage desk that books outside carriers.
dossier.why_now: Opened a second terminal this summer.

stories.industry: transportation, logistics, supply chain and storage
stories.problem: Thousands of carrier invoices arrived every month, and the team paid them too late to get the early payment discounts carriers offered.
stories.approach: Matched carrier invoices against load records automatically and scheduled each payment inside its discount window.
stories.quote: We were leaving discount money on the table every week. Now the system pays on day nine by default.

stories.industry: transportation, logistics, supply chain and storage
stories.problem: Fuel, repair and toll invoices for a fleet of 90 trucks were keyed in by two people, and closing the month took nine working days.
stories.approach: Read fuel and repair invoices automatically, coded each one to the right truck, and sent only the exceptions to a person.
stories.result_metric: Working days to close the month
stories.quote: Close used to eat the first two weeks of every month. Now it is done before the first Friday.

size_matches.problem: Invoices could not be paid until a signed lien waiver came back, and the waivers lived in a shared inbox. Payments ran late and vendors put jobs on hold.
size_matches.approach: Tied each lien waiver to its invoice, held payment until the waiver arrived, and sent the vendor a reminder when one was missing.
size_matches.quote: We stopped getting calls from suppliers threatening to pull crews. That alone was worth it.

size_matches.industry: transportation, logistics, supply chain and storage
size_matches.problem: Thousands of carrier invoices arrived every month, and the team paid them too late to get the early payment discounts carriers offered.
size_matches.approach: Matched carrier invoices against load records automatically and scheduled each payment inside its discount window.
size_matches.quote: We were leaving discount money on the table every week. Now the system pays on day nine by default.

size_matches.problem: Supply invoices for 14 clinics were keyed in by hand at the central office, and every clinic manager approved them by email.
size_matches.approach: Collected invoices from every clinic in one place, routed approvals by location, and matched supply orders to what was received.
size_matches.result_metric: Working days to close the month
size_matches.quote: Clinic managers approve in a minute instead of digging through email. Our close takes less than half the time it did.

size_matches.problem: Raw material invoices were matched to purchase orders and receipts in spreadsheets, and supplier price changes slipped through.
size_matches.approach: Ran a three-way match on every invoice and flagged any line where the price differed from the purchase order.
size_matches.result_metric: Invoices handled per AP clerk each month
size_matches.quote: We caught a supplier billing the old steel price for three months straight. The first week paid for the year.

data.headline: How a freight team your size went from 31% to 88% of carrier discounts captured
data.dek: Bluewater pays outside carriers the way your brokerage desk does. They were paying late and missing the discounts carriers offered for paying early.
data.customer_about: A transportation and logistics company with 201 to 500 people

parallel.label: Who sends invoices
parallel.them: Outside carriers, thousands of invoices a month.
parallel.you: Outside carriers booked by your brokerage desk.

data.before: Thousands of carrier invoices landed every month. By the time each one was checked and approved, the window for the carrier's early payment discount had closed. The money was there to take, and they kept missing it.
data.after: With us, carrier invoices are matched against load records as they arrive, and each payment is scheduled inside its discount window. Over six months, the share of early payment discounts they captured went from 31% to 88%.

quote.text: We were leaving discount money on the table every week. Now the system pays on day nine by default.

data.fit: If your brokerage desk pays outside carriers, the discount math works the same way it did for Bluewater: every invoice paid inside the window is money back. The new terminal will add carriers and invoices, so it is worth setting this up before volume grows. The difference is that Coldwater also runs its own fleet, and those costs follow a separate path.
